summary: This Makefile defines a target called 'hello' three separate times, each with its own echo command. When you run 'make hello', all three rules will execute in sequence, printing three different greeting messages.

explanations.1: The double colon '::' means this is a multi-rule target — multiple definitions of 'hello' are allowed and will all run, unlike a single colon which would replace the previous definition.
explanations.2: The '@' symbol suppresses echoing the command itself; only the output of the echo command will be printed, not the 'echo' line.
explanations.4: This is a second definition of the same 'hello' target with a different command, which will also execute when you run 'make hello'.
explanations.7: This is a third definition of 'hello', demonstrating that you can chain multiple actions under one target name using the double-colon syntax.
